inputs.text: More than 58 lakh people have had their names deleted from West Bengal’s electoral rolls, while the promised tribunals to challenge those removals remain unready despite the Supreme Court’s direction. The software exists; the basic question of where hearings will happen is still being discussed. That is not a harmless procedural snag. When people’s right to vote depends on navigating a system that has not even been put in place, the burden falls hardest on those with the least time, money, and access to bureaucratic power. A right without a timely, meaningful appeal is a right the state is failing to protect.

output.main_topic: Large-scale deletion of names from West Bengal’s electoral rolls and the unready appeal tribunals
